speaker: Doctor
text: Where exactly is the pain located, and does it radiate anywhere, such as to your back or groin? Is the pain constant or does it come in waves?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain feel like it is coming from your lower abdomen or pelvis, and do you have any fever or unusual vaginal discharge? I need to know if you are experiencing any pain during a pelvic exam.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain and cramping. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Pain with urination, Burning pain during intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your symptoms and history, I suspect an infection like pelvic inflammatory disease or a urinary tract issue. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Pregnancy Test.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the urinalysis and pregnancy test are normal, we need to rule out other causes for your severe pain. REQUEST TEST: Transvaginal Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the ultrasound results are not provided, could you please describe if the pain is localized to one side of your lower abdomen, particularly the right side? Do you have any fever or notice any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Menarche at 13 years, regular menses every 28 days, lasting for 5 days. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Currently in a relationship with one male partner. Reports inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a fever, and is the pain specifically localized to the right lower quadrant of your abdomen? I need to know if you experience rebound tenderness or pain when moving your right leg.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fever (notes current temperature), no urinary frequency or urgency, no change in bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of inconsistent condom use and dysuria despite a normal urinalysis, I suspect Pelvic Inflammatory Disease. I will now request a pelvic exam to check for cervical motion tenderness and adnexal masses. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Exam

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic_Exam: Cervical_Motion_Tenderness: Present, Uterine_Tenderness: Not mentioned, Adnexal_Tenderness: Not assessed, Discharge: Purulent cervical discharge noted

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of cervical motion tenderness and purulent discharge strongly supports my suspicion of an upper genital tract infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
